user.title: Ajax DoorBell & Cameras
user.description: Address of the DoorBell, or of the Ajax NVR to add the cameras it records. Use an ONVIF account created in the Ajax app: Devices → DoorBell (or NVR) → Settings → Service → Connection via ONVIF → ONVIF users. The Operator role is enough.

data_description.host: IP address of the DoorBell or of the NVR on your network. Give it a fixed lease in your router.
data_description.username: Not your Ajax account: the local ONVIF user of the device.
data_description.port: 8080 unless you changed it in the Ajax app. The RTSP port is read from the device.

reauth_confirm.title: ONVIF account refused
reauth_confirm.description: The device at {host} refused the ONVIF account. Enter it again, or create a new one in the Ajax app.

nvr.title: Ajax NVR
nvr.description: Ajax NVR found at {host}. Each camera it records gets its own device; the DoorBell keeps its own entry. Enter the NVR's ONVIF account (Ajax app: NVR → Settings → Service → Connection via ONVIF). If you already entered it in the DoorBell's options, leave the password empty.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the device. Check the address and that ONVIF is enabled in the Ajax app.
error.invalid_auth: The device refused this ONVIF account.
error.no_profiles: The device answers ONVIF but shares no video stream with this account.
error.is_nvr: This is the Ajax NVR's address, not this DoorBell's.
error.not_nvr: This address is not an Ajax NVR (no recordings).
error.password_required: Enter the ONVIF password: no DoorBell has it saved for this NVR.

abort.already_configured: This device is already set up.
abort.nvr: This is an Ajax NVR, not a DoorBell.
abort.not_video_device: This Ajax device has no ONVIF service (probably a hub).
abort.wrong_device: This address belongs to another device.

data_description.ring_duration: How long a ring waits for an answer before it counts as missed.
data_description.call_timeout: A call nobody hangs up ends by itself after this time.
data_description.nvr_host: The Ajax NVR that records the DoorBell, to replay visits from it. Nothing is stored in Home Assistant. Leave empty without an NVR.
data_description.nvr_port: ONVIF port of the NVR (8080 by default).
data_description.nvr_username: Leave empty to use the DoorBell's ONVIF account.
data_description.nvr_password: Leave empty to use the DoorBell's ONVIF account.
data_description.visit_retention: How many days of rings and people stay listed for replay.

data_description.detection_retention: How many days of motion and people stay listed for each camera, to find and replay them. The video itself stays on the NVR.

error.nvr_cannot_connect: The NVR does not answer at this address.
error.nvr_invalid_auth: The NVR refuses this ONVIF account. Create it on the NVR too (Ajax app, NVR settings, ONVIF).
error.nvr_not_nvr: This device has no recordings (ONVIF Profile G): is it the NVR?
error.nvr_no_recording: The NVR has no recording of this DoorBell.

invalid_auth.message: The DoorBell refused the ONVIF account.

no_doorbell.message: No loaded Ajax DoorBell matches this target.

answer.name: Answer
answer.description: Marks the call as answered: the ringing stops on every screen.

answered_by.name: Answered by
answered_by.description: Name of the screen or person who answered, shown on the other screens.

event_permission.title: {name}: no access to doorbell events
event_permission.description: The DoorBell shows its video to the ONVIF account but refuses its event subscription, so rings and detections do not reach Home Assistant. In the Ajax app, give this ONVIF user the Operator role (Devices → DoorBell → Settings → Service → Connection via ONVIF → ONVIF users). This message disappears by itself once events flow again.
